newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures firm, lifted by strong bullion.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures firm, lifted by strong bullion.

text.p: Yen-based gold futures edged up to end mostly at the day's highs on Wednesday, buoyed by strong bullion prices and the dollar's gains against the yen, traders said.
The most active, benchmark August, rose by 10 yen per gram to 1,377 yen, the highest level for the benchmark since February 15 this year. Other contracts ranged from eight to 10 yen per gram better.
Spot gold was quoted at $383.90/384.20 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $383.90/384.40 in New York on Tuesday and against Tuesday's Tokyo close of $381.90/382.20.
Traders said sentiment in the bullion market was firm as investment funds continued to cover their short positions.
"The gold market is currently reacting to U.S. stocks. If the Dow industrial average falls below $6,000, spot gold could probe upper resistance at $385.5," a trading house trader said.
He added that if gold managed to breach that resistance point, further short-covering could trigger a further rally.
In the gold futures market, private investors liquidated their longs in nearbys, while placing fresh buying, backed by the yen's easier tendency.
Other precious metal futures ended firmer in tandem with gold.
In platinum futures market, fresh buying in distant months was detected, while traders bought spot platinum in arbitrage.
Silver futures ranged from 0.1 yen to 2.2 yen per 10 grams firmer, with benchmark August ending up 1.9 yen at 183.0 yen.
Platinum futures ranged from three to nine yen per gram up. Benchmark August was up nine at 1,391 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from one to six yen per gram firmer. Benchmark August was up five at 430 yen. -- Tokyo Commodity Desk +81-3-3432-7431
